label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: ours is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/big_rock.mdl, models/testsphere.mdl, models/gib_legbone.mdl: the judge does not know which

M1.reason: All ten views in sides.png show a plain rectangular box: a 32x24 rectangle from front, left, back and right, and a 32x32 square from top and below. The brief asks for a valve wheel, which should show a round rim with spokes and a hub, open between the spokes. None of that is there in any view.

M2.reason: The measured size is 32 x 32 x 24, so the 32 across the brief asks for is met (sizeOff 0). But the box is 24 thick, and a 32-across valve wheel is a thin disc a few units deep. The bulk is far off a wheel's even though the one given dimension is right.

M3.reason: None of a valve wheel's parts are there: no rim, no spokes, no hub, no stem or mounting. It is a single solid box with six flat faces.

M4.reason: Every face is the same flat mid-grey with a faint concrete-like mottle. The brief asks for red paint worn to bare steel at the rim. There is no red anywhere and nothing reads as painted or bare steel.

M5.reason: There is no wear at the rim, no edge where paint gives way to steel, and no grip ridges, bolts or casting marks. The surface is one uniform mottled grey on all faces.

M6.reason: In lineup.png, B is an untextured-looking grey cube. Beside Half-Life's bone gib, rock and test sphere, it reads at once as a placeholder box. No player would take it for one of the game's props, and nothing about it says valve wheel.

M7.reason: A box has no front, no wheel face and no axis. Nothing shows which way it faces or whether it is mounted upright or lying flat as a valve wheel would be.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors, and 12 triangles is far under twice the median of 62. The box is closed, faces outward in every view and sits on the ground plane, not floating.
